name: float-function
title: A drawing helper as a float function
summary: A heart-rate sparkline whose lowest, highest and latest readings are marked by one helper, pin(i, size, sx, sy), defined once with createFloatFunction: it looks up the reading, draws a ringed dot and the value label, and is called three times with callFloatFunction.
prompt: A heart-rate line chart for today (14 readings) with the lowest (55), highest (95) and latest (64) readings marked with a red dot and their value, the latest one larger; draw the marker with one reusable helper.
teaches: Define a helper once with {"createFloatFunction": {"name": "pin", "params": ["i", "size", "sx", "sy"], "commands": [...]}}: the params are plain names in the body's expressions
Call it with {"callFloatFunction": {"id": "@pin", "args": [6, 3, "@px", "@py"]}}: one call per marker, the latest one bigger (args [13, 5, …])
Read outer data in the body (arrayGet(@bpm, i)) so a call passes only what differs (which point, how big) plus the chart's scale (@px, @py, from componentWidth()/componentHeight())
Let a function return its result by drawing: the body's draw commands run at each call site, in order with the surrounding commands
pitfalls: A variable command inside the body is a new local binding, not an assignment: a function cannot set an outer variable (the Java parser restores the variables after the body), so return values by drawing, or compute them as expressions at the call site
Paint changes made in the body stay in effect after the call: set colours inside the function, and again after it if later commands need another one
Arguments are positional: args must list a value for every param, in the params order
An expression argument ("arrayLength(@bpm) - 1") converts and runs, but rc-inspect's audit then reports it as dead_code: the audit does not yet count function arguments as uses

Pass size-dependent values to the function as arguments (here the scale @px, @py): a body that reads componentWidth(), or a variable computed from it, breaks the C++ player's later drawing in the same canvas (the line and the right-aligned label vanish); TS draws it right

snippets.note: pin(i, size, sx, sy): ring, dot and value label at reading i, placed with the scale passed in
call for the latest reading: args [13, 5, @px, @py]
the line: one segment per pair of readings, px apart

check.describe: A red line over 14 readings; red dots with dark rings and labels at 55 (third point), 95 (seventh) and a larger one at 64 (last). The C++ and TS players render it the same. Resized (narrow 240, large 540×260) the line spans the canvas: px = (componentWidth() - 48) / 13 per reading and py = (componentHeight() - 70) / 60 per bpm, passed to pin as its sx, sy arguments, so the markers stay on the line.
